title: Scan cycle and one-scan memory
summary: Follow how one input produces the current output and a copy delayed by one scan.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how fast a real controller scans or how a real button bounces.
objectives: See that a variable keeps its value from one scan to the next.
Build a one-scan delay and a one-scan pulse from a single memory.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/ScanSnapshot.st, Button is the input and Current, Delayed and RisingPulse are the outputs. Current already copies Button; Delayed and RisingPulse need to know what Button was on the previous scan.
stages.checkpoint: You can say which value a memory variable holds when a scan starts.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict the four recorded samples as Current, Delayed, RisingPulse.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starter has no one-scan memory, so RisingPulse stays FALSE at {{t:10}} ms and Delayed stays FALSE at {{t:20}} ms. Make Delayed show Button one scan late, and make RisingPulse TRUE only on the scan in which Button turns on. Declare the memory you need yourself.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named ScanSnapshot and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Compare {{t:10}}, {{t:20}}, and {{t:30}} ms: RisingPulse lasts one scan and Delayed keeps the delayed copy.
stages.checkpoint: The pulse appears at {{t:10}} ms; Delayed appears at {{t:20}} ms and returns OFF at {{t:30}} ms.

stages.title: What Check looks at
stages.body: The scenario looks at the three outputs at {{t:0}}, {{t:10}}, {{t:20}} and {{t:30}} ms, at the scan in which RisingPulse and Delayed turn on and off, and at one combination that must never happen: Delayed and RisingPulse TRUE in the same scan.
stages.checkpoint: You can say why Delayed and RisingPulse are never TRUE in the same scan.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: What would RisingPulse do if the memory were updated first, at the top of the program?
stages.checkpoint: The memory would already hold the Button of this scan, so RisingPulse would never turn on: a memory keeps the previous value only until the line that updates it.

hints.text: Delayed has to be the Button of the previous scan, so it needs a variable that still holds the old value when the scan starts: Previous.
Write the statements in this order: Current := Button; Delayed := Previous; RisingPulse := Current AND NOT Delayed; and only then Previous := Button.

faultCases: The starter has no one-scan memory, so RisingPulse stays FALSE at {{t:10}} ms and Delayed stays FALSE at {{t:20}} ms.
